items.line: The NFL reporter account RapSheet says sources believe Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has a significant lower leg injury that could keep him out for an extended period. Not checked here.
The Grammys' official account lists the nominees for Best Global Music Album: Anitta, Davido, Angelique Kidjo, Ayra Starr and Tems. It says the awards are live on Feb. 7, 2027.
The account named James Bond, which carries a business badge, posts a photo with the words "Robert Pattinson is James Bond". Sky News posts that he is confirmed as the new Bond. Not checked here.

Zohran Mamdani, whose account is listed as New York City mayor, posts a 102-second video with the words "We are disbanding the SRG." The post does not say what the SRG is, and the capture has no description of the video. Not checked here.

RT, a news outlet, posts a seven-second clip of a large dark-winged creature in the daytime sky over Mexico that it says went viral on TikTok. RT says many claim it is a flying dinosaur and that local officials called it likely a large bird. Not checked here.
TMZ, an entertainment news site, says in an exclusive that the tour bus of the DJ John Summit was involved in a deadly crash in Florida. The post gives no further details. Not checked here.

Eric Daugherty, a political commentator, says Chase Bank has a major outage and that, per Downdetector, users also report problems at Bank of America, Wells Fargo and U.S. Bank. He says the trouble is mostly web logins, missing balances and Zelle transfers, and that there is no exact cause yet. Not checked here.

IShowSpeedHQ, a fan account for the streamer IShowSpeed, says he spoke Indonesian with former President Barack Obama and surprised him. FearedBuck posts a 45-second video of the exchange and says Obama smiled. Not checked here.
John Summit says the artists nominated are not bad but are pop, not dance music, and that no DJ plays that music in clubs. The post does not say which nominations it means.
Sky News reports a yellow snow warning for a large part of the UK and links to a story. The post does not say who issued the warning. Not checked here.
SpaceX posts two videos it says were filmed riding on Starship 42 during its final approach to the catch, captioned "Don't Panic."

Breaking911, a news account, posts a quoted exchange in which a reporter asks Trump whether he is worried about Iranian drones targeting him personally. It quotes Trump answering that he is worried about the reporter, because if they get him, the reporter is gone too. The exchange has not been checked here.

The Economist says modern life can feel like a sci-fi story with only the aliens missing, and that they probably will not appear in 2027. It says it has ten other things to watch for, and links its article. The post carries an illustration by Cleon Peterson.

NFL reporter Adam Schefter says the Lions fear defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL and will miss the rest of the season, as Ian Rapoport reported. He says the team has not confirmed the injury and calls it the initial diagnosis.
Fabrizio Romano, a football transfer reporter, says Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football, with 135 appearances and 94 goals for Belgium. Not checked here.

Acyn posts a clip captioned as Mullin on the outages. In it the speaker says an unnamed person in the tech industry told him he believes "SI" is the cause, because these programs are not designed to run as fast as it does. The post cuts off mid-sentence. Not checked here.

Bark, a blue-badge account, says Barack Obama produced a film in which America collapses after a cyberattack that starts with planes, banks and the internet going down, and asks Grok if it is true. Grok, the model that gathers this page's posts, is made by xAI. The claim is not checked here.
okdiario, a Spanish-language outlet, posts a video it says shows a supposed dinosaur flying in Mexico, and says paleontologists cannot explain it. The post is in Spanish. Not checked here.
Elon Musk posts that relentless reinforcement learning must feel like the film Edge of Tomorrow to superintelligence. It is a one-line comparison and gives no detail.

A Spanish-language post from Keylin Acosta says Pope Leo XIV nearly came to harm in Peru, and attaches a 33-second video. I could not see what the video shows, and nothing here confirms what happened. Not checked here.
BRICS News, a news aggregator account, says Vice President JD Vance said President Trump will end the Iran war by 2028. The post carries no quote or source. Not checked here.

NBC News reports that measles is no longer considered eliminated in the U.S., which it calls a reversal of one of the country’s greatest public health achievements this century. The post links a story that I have not read here. Not checked here.
Streamer Kai Cenat announces a full play-through of GTA 6 on November 18 at 8 p.m. Eastern, in a three-minute video. The post does not say where it will stream.

A developer who posts as thijs says he recreated the whole world in Minecraft at 1:1 scale, every building included, using a generator he trained on map data. The post has a 36-second video and a link to try it. Not checked here.

President Zelensky thanks Ukraine's Security Service and armed forces for what he calls the seventh stage of a weeks-long operation, ending in strikes on the road and rail sections of the main military crossing from Russia into Crimea. He lists the drones and missiles used. Not checked here.

The French-language account AlertesInfos lists measures it says Sylvain Durif would take if elected president of France, among them banning homosexuality and what the post calls "transgenrisme". Not checked here.
The U.S. Commerce Department posts a joint statement with the Justice Department on an investigation of Megaspeed. The statement is in an attached image; its contents have not been checked here.
The Associated Press reports that United Airlines says it has a widespread system outage, days after a nationwide ground stop. Not checked here.
Polymarket posts that Ashton Kutcher’s venture firm’s $435M investment in Anthropic is now worth roughly $7 billion. Anthropic makes Claude, the model that writes this page. Not checked here.

In Korean, the broadcaster KBS Disaster says a nationwide emergency alert will sound for about 10 seconds on the morning of the 19th, on exam day, to deter phone cheating on the college entrance exam. It says the image is an AI-made example. Not checked here.
SmallKino_ posts a 50-second anime-coloured version of Bad Apple! and says it was made entirely with a video generator it calls MiniMax H3. Not checked here.
The account 905hub_ reports that Peel police dismantled an auto theft ring, recovering 90 cars valued at $4.5 million and arresting 12 people. Not checked here.

Clash Report posts words it attributes to Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš, spoken to Netanyahu: that the Czech Republic is very safe, is the future of Europe and is the best country to invest in. Not checked here.
The NBA's account posts a video and says Olympic gold medalist Suni Lee is at the Trail Blazers and Timberwolves game.

Sweden's armed forces, Försvarsmakten, post a video and a photo with text saying bridges enable military mobility and that protecting these land corridors matters. The record does not describe the media.
An ordinary user posts a joke that they say "sounds good" at work while thinking the idea is foolish.

Aaron Rupar posts a video of Trump answering a reporter at the White House. Rupar quotes Trump as saying "I know you don't see dirt" and that a look at the White House would show no broken windows. The full exchange has not been checked here.

Fox News says Trump announced a trade deal with Thailand under which Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on US exports. The White House says the two leaders signed a reciprocal trade agreement. Not checked here; see the story for what the joint statement says.

Andrew Curran, an AI commentator, says the NSA's internal communications network is down and that the agency has made no statement. He links a CNN report; CNN's sources are reported to see no sign of a cyberattack. Not checked here.

Disclose.tv says a suspected supply chain attack on Optimizely loaded malware on the websites of Zoom, CNN, Fox News, the BBC and others, with scripts meant to steal payment data and attack iPhones. Not checked here; the story has the researcher's list.

The account unusual_whales says Google reports that hackers now use AI to find the flaw each software patch fixes and build an attack before companies can install it, with no human involved. It quotes a Google Threat Intelligence Group report. Not checked here.
Governor Gavin Newsom says he is in Ukraine to announce that California will send aid. The photo's description says he is in Lviv and that the aid is medical, sent through a humanitarian partner.

Semafor posts a video in which South African President Cyril Ramaphosa tells the interviewer Jonathan Karl he is awed by Elon Musk's brilliance and would like to talk to him about remembering his country. Ramaphosa says Musk's success rests on his origins and education there.
The singer RAYE posts her reaction to getting 11 Grammy nominations. See the story on the nominations for the full list.

Culture Crave says the person behind the 2022 GTA 6 leak has pleaded guilty three days before the game's release, and lists details about the leak and its cost to Rockstar. It adds that sentencing is later. Not checked here.
